interaction.speaker: Ranger Maya
interaction.text: Welcome to the Friendly Zoo! Some animals are domestic - they live with people and are safe to pet gently. Wild animals live in nature and we must observe them from a distance. Let's learn the difference!

interaction.speaker: Teacher Leo
interaction.text: Remember: Domestic animals like dogs, cats, chickens, and goats are used to humans. Wild animals like bears, foxes, and wolves protect themselves. Never approach wild animals!
I thought all animals could be petted! Can you help me sort which ones are domestic and which are wild?

options.explanation: Bears are wild animals! They may look cuddly but they are dangerous and must be observed from far away.
Correct! Bears are wild animals. We stay quiet, keep distance, and observe with our eyes only.
Feeding wild animals is dangerous for you and for them. Never feed them.

interaction.question: You see a big bear behind the fence. What should you do?

options.explanation: Foxes are wild - they are not pets and can bite if scared.
options.text: Pick it up like a pet cat

options.explanation: Exactly! Foxes are wild animals. Watch silently from a distance and let a ranger care for them.
options.text: Watch from a distance and tell a ranger

options.explanation: Chasing scares wild animals and can be dangerous.

missions.title: Domestic Friends

interaction.content:
ZOO RULES:
1. DOMESTIC animals (goat, sheep, rabbit, chicken) - You may pet gently with an adult nearby, wash hands after.
2. WILD animals (bear, fox, wolf, lion) - Look with eyes only, stay behind barriers, never feed or touch, tell a ranger if animal seems sick.
interaction.title: Zoo Safety Guide

interaction.content: DOMESTIC ANIMALS live with humans. They are used to gentle touch, need food, water and shelter from people. Examples: dogs, cats, goats, rabbits, horses, chickens. How to interact: Move slowly, let them sniff your hand, pet gently on the side, be calm and quiet.
interaction.title: Domestic Animals

interaction.content: WILD ANIMALS live in nature on their own. They are NOT pets! Examples: bears, foxes, wolves, deer, tigers. How to interact: Keep distance, stay behind fences, never try to touch or feed, observe quietly, always ask a ranger.
interaction.title: Wild Animals

options.explanation: Correct! Goats, rabbits and chickens are domestic and used to people.
Bear and fox are wild animals, not domestic.
Fox is wild and should not be in the domestic group.

interaction.question: Which group contains ONLY domestic animals that you can gently interact with at the petting farm?

interaction.content: Great job! You learned: Domestic = lives with people, gentle interaction OK with care. Wild = lives in nature, observe from distance only. You are now a Zoo Helper!
interaction.title: You are a Zoo Expert!
